title: EDGE-026-overlay-risk-threshold-model
universal_lens: The overlay risk threshold model formalizes a constrained optimization manifold where financial liability is bounded by deterministic fill thresholds. It establishes a topological boundary separating permissible synthetic state spaces from prohibited real-money transactional manifolds, ensuring system stability through strict zero-leakage invariants and disabled-by-default initialization protocols.
gsi_mapping: Within GSI, this primitive acts as a conformal prediction boundary for contest participation distributions. By enforcing fake-data-first constraints, it bounds the epistemic uncertainty of user engagement models, guaranteeing that probabilistic projections of future paid versions remain strictly isolated from live production data leakage.
gse_mapping: In GSE, the model dictates a hard state-transition veto mechanism. The situational reasoning engine continuously evaluates the current repository branch and dirty state against legal boundary conditions, automatically triggering a rollback if any feature flag attempts to instantiate live leaderboards or deposit flows without explicit authorization.

primitives.name: Legal Boundary Enforcement Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: Do not launch paid contests, prizes, deposits, payouts, live leaderboards, sportsbook/DFS affiliate flows, or real-money entries without founder/legal approval.
primitives.assumptions: All real-money interactions are inherently high-risk and require explicit, external authorization vectors.
primitives.breakdown_regime: System failure if the veto kernel is bypassed, resulting in unauthorized deployment of gambling mechanics into the production environment.

layer2.mapping: Functions as a GSE state-machine guard clause, returning a fatal exception if the current action vector intersects with the set of prohibited financial flows.

primitives.name: Data Boundary Isolation Primitive
primitives.verbatim_quote: Do not import real friend-history data without explicit consent and deletion controls.
primitives.assumptions: Real-world social graphs possess non-zero privacy risk; synthetic data perfectly mimics structural properties without exposing PII.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Privacy breach occurs if the isolation boundary degrades, allowing unconsented historical data to contaminate the synthetic testing environment.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI's differential privacy mechanisms, ensuring that the gradient of any inference drawn from the test environment reveals zero information about actual users.
layer2.telemetry: Volume of PII detected in sandbox environments.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This primitive inherits its structural logic from classical actuarial science and modern regulatory compliance frameworks. Historically, risk thresholding emerged from insurance mathematics, specifically the calculation of ruin probabilities under bounded liability. In the context of software engineering, it parallels the concept of circuit breakers in distributed systems, designed to prevent cascading failures during extreme load. The specific application to fantasy sports and DFS affiliate flows reflects a contemporary synthesis of financial regulation and agile development, adapting legacy risk management principles to dynamic, real-time digital environments.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The decision actors in this model include the platform operator, the regulatory body, and the end-user. The operator seeks to maximize engagement while minimizing legal exposure, leading to a preference for synthetic testing. The regulatory actor imposes hard constraints, functioning as an external veto mechanism. The end-user, unaware of the underlying risk models, expects seamless interaction. The primitive must anticipate adversarial behavior from operators attempting to bypass safety checks for rapid growth, hence the strict enforcement of feature flags and the prohibition of real-money flows without explicit, high-level authorization.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Anti-collinearity is enforced by ensuring that the risk threshold layer operates independently of the core game logic. If the growth-os-v2 module attempts to inject real friend-history data into the contest format lab, the data boundary primitive immediately triggers a veto. This prevents any collinear alignment between user privacy violations and business expansion goals. Leakage is further prevented by mandating that all testing artifacts use fake data, creating a mathematical firewall. The system continuously validates that no secrets, live prizes, or entry fees exist in the development branch, ensuring that the risk model remains robust against internal misconfigurations or malicious insider threats.
